overview.text:
Thanjavur (Thanjai, old Tanjore) lies in the Cauvery delta about 350 km south-west of Chennai and was the capital of the Cholas, paramount in the south from the 9th to the 12th century. Their masterpiece, the Brihadeeswara or Big Temple, was completed in 1010 under Rajaraja I and is part of UNESCO's Great Living Chola Temples; its granite tower rises 216 ft over a monolithic Nandi.

The later Maratha palace holds a museum of bronzes and royal regalia beside the Saraswathi Mahal library. Thanjavur is also a home of gold-foil Thanjavur painting, of Bharatanatyam — refined here by the 18th-century Thanjavur Quartet — and of bronze casting, silk and dolls. Eat Thalappakatti biryani. Tiruchirappalli airport is about 61 km away; December to February avoids the heat.
